subject: Social Media
title: Friendster
description: A fast breakdown of Friendster for builders.

hook.text: Friendster launched in 2002 and gained 3 million users in months. Then the servers crashed. Constantly.

buildup.text: It was the first site where your real identity mattered online. People used real names and real photos.

discovery.text: Friendster proved real-identity networks could work. Millions wanted to connect. The demand was massive.

twist.text: Technical problems killed it. Pages took 40 seconds to load. Users left for a copycat that worked: MySpace.

climax.text: Friendster survived in Asia until 2015 as a gaming site. In the U.S., it became a cautionary tech tale.

punchline.text: Friendster had the right idea and the wrong servers.

quiz.question: What killed Friendster in the U.S.?
